Hi Samantha — great call today, thanks for walking through the use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Stakeholders (as discussed)
- Economic buyer: Raj Patel (CFO) — will own the budget and exec sign-off
- Procurement: procurement@finovatebank.com — expects SOW + pricing + standard T&C redlines
- Security / InfoSec: Anita Shah <anita.shah@finovatebank.com> (or security@finovatebank.com) — will require SOC 2 / architecture review
- Legal: legal@finovatebank.com — contract redlines once procurement confirms scope

Decision criteria you flagged
- Predictable per-token economics and predictable latency for peak hours
- Data isolation options / VPC deployment for regulated workflows
- SLA & audit logs for compliance reviews

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) I’ll share a draft SOW + security overview by Monday (attached) — Marissa
2) Samantha to introduce Raj + procurement contact to this thread or HubSpot record
3) Security questionnaire to be routed to Anita / security team (we can do a quick sync if helpful)
4) Aim for procurement review week of May 10, exec approval mid-May

If that aligns, I’ll attach the SOW draft and security overview for procurement/InfoSec intake. Happy to jump on a short follow-up with Raj/procurement if you want me there.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Champion enablement (talk tracks + ROI)

Samantha / team — quick note from Rishi to help Samantha (our internal champion) with a short talk track and ROI bullets she can use with Raj/procurement:

Elevator (15-30s):
- "Redwood provides a predictable, production-grade inference platform that reduces per-request cost through caching and batching optimizations while offering VPC deployment and audit logs to satisfy regulated workflows."

Top ROI bullets (to surface to Finance / Procurement):
- 30-40% projected unit-cost reduction vs current public endpoints (for our average request mix) through batching + KV caching
- Predictable reserved capacity option to smooth peak costs (Dedicated) and avoid overage surprises
- SLA-backed uptime and audit logs to reduce compliance review cycles (faster procurement/implementation)

Suggested ask for procurement call:
- Confirm target monthly commit and whether they'd prefer Dedicated (reserved) or Hosted + burst option.
- Ask for a short procurement checklist: required docs, target approval date, and primary contact for redlines.

If useful, I can join the pricing walkthrough with Raj for 15 mins. Happy to be on the technical 30-min call for InfoSec as well.

— Rishi
